whatWorks: The ground and the bone value are right. Near-black ground with a warm bone mass reads as monument rather than as diagram, and it holds the twelve tiles together as one collection at 120px without any tile shouting. This register is the single most on-brief thing here and must not be traded away for contrast.

The stress column proves the runtime can already draw the target image. 5003 stress and 5134 stress are quiet, compact, uninterrupted single masses on a mostly empty field, and they are the closest any frame on these sheets comes to the STELE brief. Whatever else changes, that austerity must survive as a reachable state.

Between silhouette families the identity work is real. At 120px a circle seed (5134, 6182), a triangle seed (5265, 5920) and a diamond/star seed (5789, 6313) are unmistakably not each other, so the outer contour is already carrying seed identity rather than colour or texture doing it.

The stroke-only nested generations, clearest in 5396, 6444 and 6051, read as recursion rather than as ornament. An outlined generation sitting inside a filled parent is a legible way to say one generation inside the last, and it does not depend on interior detail resolving at browse size.

findings.whatFails: Across every row of the states sheet the market changes element count, not size. 5134 neutral is a circle carrying squares and small discs; 5134 stress is the same diameter circle with the interior stripped nearly bare; 5134 recovery is the same circle with satellites added far outside it. 5003 and 5396 do the same thing, and 5265 recovery simply gains fragments. The mass does not contract under drawdown and does not grow in recovery; only the amount of stuff on it moves.
findings.why: The brief asks for exactly the opposite: the market changes the form's scale rather than its complexity, so the work reads as one object breathing rather than as a composition rearranging itself. As built, stress is the state where the piece looks most like the brief and recovery is the state where it looks least like it, which inverts the intent and makes drawdown read as calm and recovery as clutter.
findings.specificChange: Bind the market sensor to a single uniform scale factor applied to the whole nested figure about a fixed centroid, and pin generation count, element count and every per-generation transform to the seed so they are byte-identical across neutral, stress and recovery. Target roughly 0.65x mass diameter at stress, 1.0x at neutral and 1.2x at recovery, and remove the market's influence on how many primitives are drawn entirely.
findings.keep: Keep the austerity that the stress renders currently have. 5003 stress and 5134 stress should become the baseline look of the neutral state, not a state that is only reachable under drawdown; the fix must move that cleanliness into all three states rather than deleting it along with the complexity binding.

findings.whatFails: Small primitives sit outside the main mass and touch nothing: the two floating squares in 5003, the small discs above and below the circle in 5134, the two diamonds flanking 5789 at left and right, the corner blobs in all four corners of 5658, the fragments off the right edge of 5920, and the whole scatter added by 5003 and 5134 in recovery. At 120px these read as dirt on the tile rather than as part of the object.
findings.why: The direction is one dominant mass and nothing else of consequence, with any inner structure subordinate to the single silhouette. A detached fragment is by definition not inner structure and not subordinate; it converts a single placed object into a small constellation, which is the composition rearranging itself that the brief explicitly rules out.
findings.specificChange: Remove every primitive whose bounding box is not fully contained inside its parent generation's bounding box, and constrain each generation to be inscribed within the previous one so the recursion can only ever step inward. Nothing may be emitted outside the outermost generation's contour.
findings.keep: Keep the outlined, stroke-only inner generations that currently sit inside the mass. They are the clearest recursion cue on the sheet and they are already contained; the containment rule must prune the escapees without flattening the interior to a solid blank.

findings.whatFails: Several tokens are neither small nor centred. 5658 fills its whole tile and is clipped at the top edge, the bottom edge and all four corners; 6313 is cut off at the bottom of the frame; 5134's upper satellite touches the top edge; 6182 nearly fills its tile edge to edge. Placement drifts too, with 5003 sitting left of centre, 5396 high and right, and 6444 pushed to the right of its tile.
findings.why: The composition and density directions both demand the single form be held well clear of every edge, occupying well under half the frame, with the surrounding emptiness doing as much work as the mass. A clipped form is read as a crop of something larger, which destroys the sense of a placed object; and a form filling the tile removes the negative space that the brief says is the reason it reads as placed at all.
findings.specificChange: Pin a hard cap on the union bounding box of every drawn primitive at 45 percent of the shorter frame dimension, computed before drawing, then centre that union bounding box on the frame centre and scale the whole figure down until at least a 20 percent margin exists on all four sides. No primitive may extend past the cap.
findings.keep: Keep the per-seed variation in how large the mass is within that cap. 5265 and 6444 are already small and quiet against a lot of ground, and the fix must not normalise every token to one uniform diameter; scale variation between seeds is legitimate as long as every seed clears the margin.

findings.whatFails: Overlapping translucent fills are manufacturing a smooth ramp of greys rather than two values. 5003, 5527 and 5920 each show six or more distinct tones inside one mass, produced purely by how many translucent shapes happen to stack; 6051's circle shows a soft mid-grey lobe where two discs cross; the 512 single shows a bone triangle, a mid-grey triangle, a charcoal triangle and two further intermediate tones from overlap.
findings.why: The palette intent is two values and a ground, bone against charcoal over near black, nothing decorative and no third colour anywhere. Tones that appear because shapes happen to cross are incidental by construction, and the brief bans texture that is not structural. The ramp also flattens the figure into a soft haze at 120px instead of a crisp silhouette.
findings.specificChange: Replace alpha compositing with opaque fills drawn back to front, and declare exactly two fill values, bone and charcoal, over the near-black ground. Forbid any tone that is not one of those three, so overlap resolves as occlusion rather than as blending, and let a generation differ from its parent by alternating between the two declared values.
findings.keep: Keep the near-black ground and the exact bone value already in use, and keep alternating value between successive generations as the way inward steps are read. The fix is to stop overlap from inventing tones, not to reduce the piece to a single flat value.

findings.whatFails: At 120px the twelve seeds collapse into three families of four rather than twelve works. 5265, 5920 and 6444 are all a rightward-pointing triangle with a nested triangle and differ mainly in size; 5134, 6182 and 6051 are all a large disc with small marks on it; 5789 and 6313 are both a diamond with points. Within a family the outer contour is effectively the same image at browse size.
findings.why: The variation strategy says tokens differ first in the silhouette of the single form, then in symmetry, then in generation count, and the thumbnail intent says one compact silhouette must read immediately as a single object with interior steps not resolving. If interior steps are correctly not resolving, and the outer contour repeats across four seeds, then four seeds are one work at the size the collection is actually browsed at.
findings.specificChange: Widen the outer generation to a regular n-gon with n drawn per seed across 3 through 8, and spread a per-seed rotation offset and a per-seed symmetry order across the full legal range so the outer contour is a seed-driven structural choice rather than a pick from three base primitives. Drive silhouette from those two parameters before any interior parameter is drawn.
findings.keep: Keep the between-family separation that already works. A circle seed, a triangle seed and a diamond seed are genuinely different at 120px today, and that distinctness is the floor the widened set has to clear, not something to average away by making every silhouette a similar mid-sided polygon.

overall: The register is right and the mechanism is bound to the wrong axis. Ground, bone value and the general austerity of the palette already read as monument, and the stress column shows the runtime can produce very nearly the brief's picture on demand. But the market is driving complexity instead of scale, so drawdown strips the piece to its most on-brief state and recovery buries it in satellites, which is the inverse of one object breathing. Underneath that, three things fight the brief at browse size: primitives escaping the mass and reading as dirt, several tokens filling or clipping their tile instead of sitting well clear of every edge, and alpha overlap manufacturing a continuum of greys where two values were specified. Seed identity is real between silhouette families and absent within them, so twelve seeds currently browse as about three works. The corrections are mostly subtractive and mostly compatible: pin element count to the seed and give the market scale alone, contain every generation inside its parent, cap and centre the union bounding box, drop to opaque two-value fills, and push the per-seed variation into the outer contour where the thumbnail can see it.
